Direct answer｜The work of gambling surveillance officers and gambling investigators can be broadly divided into three categories. First, observation and anomaly identification: use audio and video equipment and one-way mirrors to continuously observe casino or casino hotel operations and identify irregular activity such as cheating or theft by employees or patrons, monitor establishment activity to ensure compliance with the gambling regulations of the jurisdiction and company policies and procedures, and check and monitor audio or video surveillance equipment to ensure it is working properly and review video surveillance recordings. Second, investigation and documentation: investigate potential threats to gambling assets such as money and chips and gambling equipment, verify transactions and game procedures and construct an incident timeline, establish and maintain a surveillance observation log, preserve video and logs and evidence, and report violations and suspicious behavior orally or in writing according to authorization. Third, supervision and collaboration and training: act as oversight and security agents for management and customers, train or supervise surveillance observers, and collaborate according to procedures with security and compliance and management positions. The three categories of work link in cycles: continuous observation and equipment checks — identify anomalies and verify procedures — preserve evidence and record logs — produce reports and escalate according to authorization.

O*NET occupational profile highlights｜The official scope of O*NET-SOC 33-9031.00 “Gambling Surveillance Officers and Gambling Investigators” is: Observe gambling operation for irregular activities such as cheating or theft by either employees or patrons. Investigate potential threats to gambling assets such as money, chips, and gambling equipment. Act as oversight and security agent for management and customers. All 8 tasks given in the occupational profile are core tasks: monitor establishment activity to ensure compliance with all applicable jurisdictional gambling regulations and company policies and procedures; use audio and video equipment and one-way mirrors to observe irregular activity in casino or casino hotel operations (such as cheating or theft by employees or patrons); report all violations and suspicious behavior to supervisors orally or in writing; establish and maintain a surveillance observation log; check and monitor audio or video surveillance equipment to ensure it is working properly; review video surveillance recordings; act as an oversight or security agent for management or customers; and train or supervise surveillance observers. subject.summary: Gambling Surveillance Officers and Gambling Investigators (O*NET-SOC 33-9031.00, Gambling Surveillance Officers and Gambling Investigators) observe irregular activity in gambling operations within licensed gambling establishments and investigate potential threats to gambling assets, acting as oversight and security agents for management and customers: using audio and video equipment and one-way mirrors to continuously observe casino or casino hotel operations and identify cheating or theft by employees or patrons; monitoring establishment activity to ensure compliance with the gambling regulations of the jurisdiction and company policies and procedures; checking and monitoring audio or video surveillance equipment to ensure it is working properly; reviewing video surveillance recordings; investigating potential threats to gambling assets such as money and chips and gambling equipment; verifying transactions and game procedures and constructing an incident timeline; establishing and maintaining a surveillance observation log; preserving video and logs and evidence; reporting violations and suspicious behavior to supervisors orally or in writing; and training or supervising surveillance observers. Official definition text: Observe gambling operation for irregular activities such as cheating or theft by either employees or patrons. Investigate potential threats to gambling assets such as money, chips, and gambling equipment. Act as oversight and security agent for management and customers.
